output.name: Thuskal
output.myth: When the Reel was still tight, the drowned came up out of the Leeward water and stood on the skerries with their arms held out, the way shags stand at low tide to dry their wings. Kael was casting for fallen stars and caught nothing, but he saw them and came home quiet. The Lamp Boat, north-east of here, keeps a lantern for every name said at the harbour mouth, and it burned brighter that night, as if someone had counted. Halvun the Ray That Flies saw them first from the dark south-west, and she is no fish, so she does not hide what she saw. They must dry before they fly north to the Spindle, where Mother Hesk is still winding. Tavo the Gale came over the rocks and laughed, which is why some wings are torn at the edge. The rule is old and plain. If you see the shag-shapes on the black rock, do not look long. Turn your face to the mending and count your knots. Hesk keeps count of who looked, and she is patient, and so is the sea.
output.finding: Find The Lamp Boat, then look about one fist (9°) to its south-west, where the shag-shapes stand low on the black rock.
